name: Melanie Arendt
life: “I still remember my family keeping sweets in a medicine bottle.” Friday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Melanie takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I fitted a pocket for the tablets he won't carry. He keeps boiled sweets in it for my grandchildren.
appearance: Melanie has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for short black hair swept back. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a dark green knitted vest with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. In conversation Melanie turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Melanie has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Melanie knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To fit a pocket that can hold medicine or treats.
family: Winifred Starr is Melanie’s stepsibling. Melanie asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Winifred remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The pawned trumpet*, Winifred says, “I'm the downstairs dealer everyone suspected of taking it.”
connections: Merritt Parker. A pocket and an unequal sleeve solve two different problems in a familiar shirt.

reactions.situation: A staff supervisor demands the stranger's laundry back
reactions.response: Melanie checks with the shirt's owner before handing it over to anyone else.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Melanie walks with the bystander to a staffed doorway and checks whether they want someone called.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Melanie asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
